Definition: to be able, literally (can, could) or morally (may, might)
BiblicalUsage: Yâkôl is the ordinary word for being able, whether of strength or of permission. David could not go before the ark to enquire of God because he was afraid, and Solomon asked for an understanding heart because he knew no man is able to judge so great a people on his own.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the honest confession of what I cannot do is the beginning of wisdom, and Solomon prayed it before he ever ruled.
